title: deps: the daily OSV scan is red — next 16.4.1 (GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h, GHSA-vc7v-qv4w-wrv8; fixed in 16.4.5) and picomatch 4.0.7 (GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf, 8.7, no patched version)
body:
triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

Filed by triage (R1210). The scheduled **Validate Dependencies** run is red on `main`: run 44227606138 (2026-11-18 03:02Z), and also 11-17 03:02Z.

## What the scan reports (public advisories, `pnpm-lock.yaml`)
| Advisory | CVSS | Package | Installed | Fixed |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h | 6.3 | next | 16.4.1 | 16.4.5 |
| GHSA-vc7v-qv4w-wrv8 | 6.3 | next | 16.4.1 | 16.4.5 |
| GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf | 8.7 | picomatch | 4.0.7 | none yet |

`next` is declared only by `apps/docs/package.json`, the docs site, not the shipped runtime.

## Done when
1. Bump `next` to ≥ 16.4.5 in `apps/docs`, and the lockfile resolves it.
2. For `picomatch`: find which package pulls 4.0.7 and whether its vulnerable path is reachable. Bump it if a non-breaking version exists. Otherwise add a reasoned filter in `osv-scanner.toml`, the way the minimatch entry (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249) is justified, naming the dependent and why it is not reachable.
3. The next scheduled Validate Dependencies run is green.

Grade: **p1 · domain:devx**. Theme: performance and security. A red daily dependency scan on `main` is graded p1 by precedent (#32386, #33211). It goes to repo:objectstack#1, the p1 seat.
